audit_findings.title: Gross cash bridge may include seller-owned funds
audit_findings.magnitude: $72.244 million of filed payables to sellers, equal to approximately $2.00 per diluted share, 31.3% of the $231.099 million cash-and-investments bridge, and 11.6% of base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: For consignment sales transactions, funds are typically collected from buyers and are held by the Company on the sellers' behalf.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that seller funds are included in cash and that $72.244 million was payable to sellers at June 30, 2026. Thus, treating the entire cash balance as distributable is an error in concept. The precise adjustment remains unresolved because the record does not reconcile individual seller-fund balances between payables to sellers, accounts payable, restricted amounts, and cash. Deducting just the filed payables-to-sellers balance would reduce base value by about $2.00 per share, a material change to the valuation even though value would remain well below the $42.105 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 30, 2026 seller collections to the $72.244 million payables-to-sellers balance, relevant portions of the $60.636 million accounts payable balance, restricted cash, and subsequent settlements; rerun every scenario and buy-below price using only cash economically available to common equity.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may capitalize a temporary purchase-model surge
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 anchor OE of $27.8 million; nine-month FY2026 RSCG direct profit increased $13.549 million, or 24.9%, while purchase revenue decreased $0.117 million
audit_findings.evidence: Revenue from our RSCG reportable segment increased by $97.3 million, or 41.8%, concentrated in the first three quarters of fiscal 2025, due to a $97.7 million, or 30.5%, increase in GMV from expanded multi-channel buyer development efforts with existing and new retail client programs alike, and increased volumes from our client purchase model programs relative to our consignment programs, while certain inventory purchases were reduced starting in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The cited FY2025 revenue surge was real, but the subsequent filed results do not demonstrate that it temporarily inflated sustainable earnings. Through June 2026, RSCG purchase revenue was essentially flat to slightly lower, yet RSCG direct profit rose from $54.434 million to $67.983 million and consolidated operating income rose $9.021 million. Nine-month FY2026 net income of $25.437 million also already approached the full-year $27.8 million OE anchor. The post-surge record therefore supports, rather than undermines, the anchor at the scale relevant to this valuation.
audit_findings.action: Complete FY2026 OE from the fourth-quarter filing and rerun only if full-year OE or normalized RSCG direct profit falls materially below the $27.8 million anchor.

audit_findings.title: Mandatory inventory-purchase commitments may be an unrecognized senior operating claim
audit_findings.mechanism: future OE and working-capital cash requirements, with any unavoidable loss also reducing the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: In our RSCG segment, we are obligated under certain supply agreements to take delivery of product regardless of prevailing demand conditions, which limits our ability to adjust our inventory levels in response to fluctuations in our buyer demand.
audit_findings.explanation: The supply agreements and unconditional delivery requirement are demonstrated, but neither committed quantities nor contract economics are supplied. The record therefore cannot establish an existing loss, cash requirement, or valuation magnitude. The risk could reduce future OE or consume purported excess cash if committed inventory is above market, but that outcome remains an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the agreements and June 2026 commitment schedule; quantify minimum purchases, pricing versus current resale value, termination costs, expected inventory margins, and working-capital timing, then rerun OE and the cash bridge for any unavoidable loss or incremental funding requirement.

audit_findings.title: Outstanding letters of credit are omitted contingent claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.3 million maximum face amount, approximately $0.31 per diluted share and 1.8% of the $622 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: bridge if drawn or otherwise representing an unrecorded economic obligation
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025, the Company had no outstanding borrowings under the Line of Credit and had $9.0 million of standby letters of credit outstanding.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing establishes $11.3 million of outstanding standby letters of credit, not $9.0 million. They reduce borrowing capacity but are not themselves debt or an equity claim unless draw conditions occur and the underlying obligation produces an uncompensated loss. Even conservatively treating the entire face amount as an equity loss would lower base value only from $17.18 to about $16.87 per share and would not change the conclusion relative to the $42.105 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm beneficiaries, draw conditions, collateral, expirations, and whether underlying obligations are already recorded in accounts payable or payables to sellers; rerun the bridge only for probable exposure not already recognized.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash requires a repatriation-access and tax adjustment
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.5 million held outside the United States, approximately $0.79 per diluted share and 4.6% of the $622 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: cash bridge through repatriation taxes or legal access restrictions
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025 and 2024, $ 22.5 million and $ 25.7 million, respectively, of cash and cash equivalents was held overseas and not available to fund domestic operations without incurring taxes upon repatriation.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing demonstrates that $28.5 million was held outside the United States and excluded from domestic near-term liquidity because repatriation may have adverse tax consequences. That does not make the cash valueless to consolidated equity, but the bridge should reflect actual tax leakage or restrictions. Even the extreme upper bound of excluding the entire $28.5 million would reduce base value from $17.18 to about $16.39 per share and leave every scenario far below the $42.105 market price; realistic tax leakage would be smaller.
audit_findings.action: Map the $28.5 million by jurisdiction and legal owner, calculate withholding and incremental U.S. or local taxes under realistic distribution routes, and deduct only the computed leakage or genuinely inaccessible amount.

audit_findings.title: Pension guarantee could become a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: £10 million contractual guarantee cap; FY2025 plan surplus of $1.577 million; June 2026 exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: future OE through required contributions or the bridge if the guarantee becomes payable
audit_findings.evidence: The Company guarantees GoIndustry's performance on all present and future obligations to make payments to the Scheme for up up up to to to a maximum of £ 10 million British pounds.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantee is a real contingent obligation, but the latest quantified actuarial record showed $15.902 million of assets against a $14.325 million obligation, leaving the plan overfunded by $1.577 million, and the company did not plan near-term contributions. No present claim or valuation adjustment is demonstrated. Funding deterioration could create future cash outflows, so the item warrants monitoring rather than a current deduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest actuarial valuation, post-September-2025 asset performance, trustee funding demands, guarantee draw provisions, and contribution schedule; rerun OE and the bridge if a deficit or probable contribution requirement emerges.
